speaker: Doctor
text: The positive Dix-Hallpike maneuver and your description of positional vertigo strongly suggest Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). To confirm which canal is affected, does the spinning sensation last for less than a minute after you change position?

speaker: Patient
text: Yes, the spinning usually stops after about 30 seconds, though I feel a bit off-balance for a while after. It never lasts longer than a minute.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you, that brief duration is classic for BPPV. Do you have any history of head trauma, recent viral infections, or do you experience any hearing loss or ringing in your ears?

speaker: Patient
text: No, I haven't had any recent head injuries or illnesses. My hearing has gradually declined with age, but I don't experience any ringing in my ears or sudden hearing changes.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the positional nature of your vertigo, the positive Dix-Hallpike test, and the absence of other neurological or auditory symptoms, I am confident in my assessment. DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV)
